rationale: The algebraic arithmetic rank of a structure measures its complexity in terms of the length of sequences of jumps in the arithmetic hierarchy. By extending this notion to Boolean circuits, we may uncover hidden complexity relationships between circuit structures and their computational difficulty. If true, this conjecture would provide a new perspective on the nature of computational hardness.
